questions.question: The principal lignite reserves are in Neyveli which is situated in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Neyveli** is a town located in the Cuddalore district of the Indian state of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It is home to one of the largest lignite reserves in the country, known as the** Neyveli Lignite Mines**.
 
• **Here are some key points to help explain the significance of Neyveli's lignite reserves:**
 
• **Size and scope:**
 
 
• The Neyveli Lignite Mines are spread over an area of** 64 square kilometers** and contain reserves of around 6,000 million tonnes of lignite.
 
• This makes it one of the largest lignite mining operations in the world.
 
 
 
• **Importance to the energy sector: **
 
 
• Lignite is a type of **coal **that is relatively** low in carbon **content and is primarily used for generating electricity.
 
 
 
• **Economic impact:**
 
 
• The Neyveli Lignite Mines is a major employer in the region, providing direct and indirect employment opportunities to thousands of people.
 
 
 
• **Environmental concerns:**
 
 
• Lignite is considered a relatively dirty form of energy due to its high carbon emissions and other environmental impacts.
 
• The mining and use of lignite at Neyveli have been criticized for their contribution to air and water pollution, as well as their impact on the local ecosystem and communities.
 
 
 
• Overall, the lignite reserves at Neyveli are an important resource for the energy sector in India, but they also raise important questions about environmental sustainability and the trade-offs between economic development and environmental protection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Types of Coal**

 
• Anthracite:

 
 
• Anthracite coal has the best coal quality.
 
• In India Anthracite found only in Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• Anthracite has more than 80% carbon content.
 
 
 
• Bituminous:
 
 
• Bituminous is the second-best quality of coal.
 
• Bituminous has 60 to 80 % Carbon Content
 
• Bituminous is the most popular coal in commercial use.
 
 
 
• Lignite:
 
 
• Lignite is a low-grade brown coal
 
• Lignite are used for the generation of electricity.
 
• The principal lignite reserves are in Neyveli in Tamil Nadu
 
 
 
• Peat :
 
 
• Peat is the poorest quality of coal.
 
• Peat has less than 40% carbon content

questions.question: Babur ruled over Delhi till ________ year.

questions.question: Which of these methods is used for conservation of land resource?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Land reclamation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Land reclamation**

 
 
• Land reclamation is the process of creating new land from the ocean, riverbeds, or lake beds.
 
• The process of reconverting disturbed land to its former or other productive uses.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Deforestation:
 
• Deforestation is the process of removing trees from forests (or other places) on a big scale in order to facilitate human actions.
 
• It is a major environmental issue.
 
• Some of the major causes of deforestation are:
 
 
• Agriculture.
 
• Logging.
 
• Mining and urban expansion.
 
 

 
• **Poaching**

 
 
• Poaching is an illegal hunting process.
 
• Poachers are illegitimate hunters who kill wild animals for their different body parts.
 
• These are some examples of animals that are killed for poaching: Crocodiles, rhinos, elephants, lions, and deer.
 
 

 
• ​Indiscriminate use of fertilizers has led to soil pollution, water pollution, and air pollution.

 
 
• Effects of excess use of fertilizers:

 
 
• Oxygen Depletion:

 
 
• When manure or commercial fertilizers enter surface water, the nutrients they release stimulate microorganism growth.
 
• The growth and reproduction of microorganisms reduce the dissolved oxygen content of the water body.
 
 
 
• Ammonia Toxicity:
 
 
• Ammonia-contaminated runoff from fresh manure application sites is toxic to aquatic life.
 
• At high levels, ammonia in surface water will kill fish.
 
• Fish are relatively sensitive to ammonia in water.

questions.question: In which of the following Indian states is the “Hundred Drums Festival” observed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Drums Festival**

 
 
• Hundred Drum Festival also known as the 'Wangala Festival, the Wangala Festival is a traditional festival in the northeastern Indian state of Meghalaya.
 
• A group of 30 dancers with 10 drums would form a group and 10 such groups will be there. 
 
• Thus, a total of 100 drummers and 300 dancers make up what is now known as the “100 Drums Wangala Festival”.
 
• Every year the festival is celebrated for 3 days during the month of November.
 
• Ordinary Garo people pay gratitude and reverence to Missi Saljong or 'Pattigipa Ra'Rongipa' (Great Giver) for blessing humans with a prosperous harvest for the season.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

__
 
• The Wangala festival marks the end of a period of toil, that brings good results to the fields which also signifies the onset of winter.
 
• It is also celebrated in honour of the Sun God that marks the end of the long harvest season.
 
• Wangala is celebrated with different forms of dance.
 
• These dances are performed on the tunes of folk songs that are played on drums and primitive flute.
 
• Additionally, these flutes are made of buffalo horns.
 
• On the first day of the festival, people celebrate it with a ceremony called Ragula.
 
• This ceremony is performed in the house of the village’s chief.
 
• Then on the second day of celebration, which is called Kakkat, people begin the ceremony by dancing to the rhythms of long oval-shaped drums
 
• In this celebration, young and old join together while men play the drums and women perform traditional dance forms. The dance form is known as Dama Dagota.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Meghalaya:

 
 
• Lok Sabha seats - 2.
 
• Rajya Sabha seats - 1.
 
• State Animal - Clouded leopard.
 
• State Bird - Common hill myna.
 
• National Parks - Balphakram National Park, Nokrek Ridge National Park.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right was deleted by The Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Property**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 44th Constitutional amendment act 1978 deleted the right to property__ from the list of Fundamental Rights.
 
• Right to Property is no more a fundamental right, only a legal right.
 
• The right to property was listed under Article 31 before its deletion.
 
• At present right to property is listed under Article 300A as a legal right.
 
• In the original constitution, there were seven categories of fundamental rights in India.
 
• After the deletion of the Right to property by the 44th Amendment, it was reduced to six.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Now there are six categories of fundamental rights in India.
 
 
• Right to Equality.
 
• Right to Freedom.
 
• Right against Exploitation.
 
• Right to Freedom of Religion.
 
• Cultural and Educational Rights.
 
• Right to Constitutional Remedies.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Fundamental rights are justiciable.
 
• The Supreme court and the High Courts are considered as the guardians of Fundamental rights in India.

questions.question: Most of the Chlorophyceae have one or more storage bodies called _______ located in the chloroplasts.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pyrenoids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pyrenoids**

 
 
• Pyrenoid is a protein-rich body found in the members of Chlorophyceae or green algae. It is used for the storage of reserved food material.
 
• It may be one to many in number in different species of algae.
 
• The chloroplast is a double membrane-bound cell organelle.
 
• Out of the two membranes, the inner membrane is relatively less permeable (the outer membrane contains porins)
 
• The number & shape of chloroplast also varies from one species of algae to another.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Stomata ​

 
 
• Stomata are the tiny pores on the leaves which play a major role in the exchange of gases.
 
• The intake of carbon dioxide and the outtake of oxygen both takes place through these pores.
 
• The respiration in leaves takes place through these tiny pores.
 
• Evaporation of water from the leaf surface occurs through the stomata.
 
• Thus, the stomata help in the process of transpiration.
 
• It also closes or opens its pores based on climatic conditions to maintain the moisture balance.
 
• It remains open during the day and closed at night. This closure at night prevents water from escaping through open pores.
 
 

 
• **Carotenoids**

 
 
• arotenoids also called tetraterpenoids, are yellow, orange, and red organic pigments__ that are produced by plants and algae, as well as several bacteria and fungi.
 
• Carotenoids give the characteristic color to pumpkins, carrots, corn, tomatoes, canaries, flamingos, salmon, lobster, shrimp, and daffodils.
 
 
 
• **Chlorophyll**
 
 
• **​**Chlorophyll or leaf green is a porphyrin derivative with magnesium (Mg) as the central atom and is hence a metal complex dye.
 
• It is present in the chloroplasts in all green parts of plants as a mixture of blue-green chlorophyll a and yellow-green chlorophyll b and constitutes the catalyst for photosynthesis.
 
• Chlorophylls are porphyrins, whose molecules contain a flat ring of four-linked heterocyclic groups, based upon magnesium.
 
• Chlorophyll is a green photosynthetic pigment found in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria.
 
 

61

questions.question: The bill which provide for the trial of British or European person by Indians was _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ilbert Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 'Ilbert Bill' was introduced in 1883 under the Viceroyship of Lord Ripon.

 
 
• Ilbert Bill was drafted by Sir Courtenay Ilbert on 9th February 1883 during the viceroyship of Lord Rippon.
 
• The main objective behind the introduction of this bill is to allow Indian judges to try cases in session courts involving Britishers.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The introduction of the bill had roused anger and resentment among people, especially English women and British tea and indigo planters in Bengal.
 
• English women argued that Bengali women were not respected by their male counterparts, so they shouldn't get the power to try cases involving Britishers.
 
• On the contrary, Bengali women who supported the bill said that they were more educated and had good academic records than English Women.

questions.question: Which of the following cities became the capital of Bengal in 1704?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Murshidabad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Murshid Quli Khan, also known as Mohammad Hadi and born as Surya Narayan Mishra, was the first Nawab of Bengal, serving from 1717 to 1727.

 
 
• Born a Hindu in the Deccan Plateau c. 1670, Murshid Quli Khan was bought by Mughal noble Haji Shafi.
 
• After Shafi's death, he worked under the Divan of Vidarbha, during which time he piqued the attention of the then-emperor Aurangzeb, who sent him to Bengal as the divan c. 1700.
 
• However, he entered into a bloody conflict with the province's subahdar, Azim-us-Shan.
 
• After Aurangzeb's death in 1707, he was transferred to the Deccan Plateau by Azim-us-Shan's father the Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah I. 
 
• The capital was shifted from Dhaka to Murshidabad.

questions.question: Iron, iodine and zinc can be considered as which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Micronutrients**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Macronutrients**__ in animal nutrition include carbohydrates, proteins, and fats, which are required in large amounts for energy, growth, and maintenance of body functions.

 __
 
• Minerals such as calcium, phosphorus, and magnesium are also considered** macrominerals. **
 
• Since iron, iodine, and zinc are required in much smaller amounts than these macronutrients, they do not fall into this category.
 
 
 
• Micronutrient__
 __
 
• Micronutrients are nutrients required in much smaller amounts compared to macronutrients.​
 
• **Iron (Fe):** Iron is a critical component of hemoglobin, which is responsible for oxygen transport in the blood. It is also part of various enzymes and proteins involved in energy production and metabolism. A deficiency of iron can lead to anemia and other health issues.
 
• **Iodine (I): **Iodine is essential for the production of thyroid hormones, which regulate metabolism, growth, and development. A deficiency in iodine can lead to goiter and hypothyroidism, affecting the overall health and metabolic rate of the animal.
 
• **Zinc (Zn)**: Zinc is involved in numerous aspects of cellular metabolism, acts as a cofactor for over 300 enzymes, and plays a role in immune function, protein synthesis, wound healing, DNA synthesis, and cell division. Zinc deficiency can impair growth, immune function, and reproduction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Steroid hormone inducers **are substances that influence the production or action of steroid hormones (like cortisol, estrogen, testosterone). This category does not apply to iron, iodine, or zinc as these minerals do not directly induce steroid hormone production.

questions.question: Who among the following is noted for playing the Flute?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia**

 
 
• Hariprasad Chaurasia is an Indian film music director and classical flutist, who plays the BANSURI, in the Hindustani classical tradition.
 
• Chaurasia was born in Allahabad (1938) (officially called Prayagraj) in the state of Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
 
• Awards
 
 
• Sangeet Natak Academy - 1984
 
• Padma Bhushan - 1992
 
• Padma Vibhushan - 2000​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pandit Kumar Gandharva**

 
 
• Pandit Kumar Gandharva was born in Belgaum, Karnataka on 8th April 1924.
 
• He was legend in the field of Hindustani classical music.
 
• Kumar Gandharva broke the traditional method of singing the Gharana (a form of classical music).
 
 

 
• Pandit Ravi Shankar (1920-2012):

 
 
• He was an Indian sitar virtuoso and a composer. 
 
• He became the world's best-known exponent of North Indian classical music, in the second half of the 20th century and influenced many other musicians throughout the world.
 
• Ravi Shankar was awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna in 1999 and received **4** Grammy Awards for his outstanding work.
 
 

 
• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma

 
 
• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was a Santoor player from the Indian state Jammu and Kashmir. 
 
• He co-produced a concept album, Call of the Valley (1967), in 1967 with flautist Hariprasad Chaurasia and guitarist Brij Bhushan Kabra.
 
• Shivkumar is the recipient of national and international awards, including honorary citizenship of Baltimore City, the USA in 1985, the 1986 Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, 1991 Padma Shri and 2001 Padma Vibhushan.

questions.question: The GDP estimation method measuring the aggregate value of goods and services produced by the firms is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**product method**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Product Method:

 
 
• Product or value added method is a way of computing the national income of a country.
 
• This system is also known as output or inventory method. This method calculates national income by adding value to a product at every stage of its production.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **expenditure method**

 
 
• The expenditure method is a system for calculating gross domestic product (GDP) that combines *consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.*
 
• It is the most common way to estimate GDP. It says everything that the private sector, including consumers and private firms, and government spend within the borders of a particular country, must add up to the total value of all finished goods and services produced over a certain period of time. 
 
 
 
• **consumption method**
 
 
• These consumption inventory methods offer a radically different method of accounting for a community's contribution to greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Traditional inventories evaluate the emissions associated with a diverse set of activities within a geographic area.​
 
 
 
• Income Method:
 
 
• In the income method, the national income is measured by adding up the pretax income generated by the individuals and companies in the economy.
 
• It consists of income from wages, rent of buildings and land, interest on capital, profits, etc.

questions.question: The Chholiya dance is performed in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chholiya dance ​

 
 
• Chholiya is a dance form which originated in the Kumaon division in the state of Uttarakhand and in some parts of Sudur Paschim province of Nepal.
 
• It has today become a symbol of Kumaoni culture.
 
 
• Kumaoni is an Indo-Aryan language spoken by over two million people of the Kumaon region of the state of Uttarakhand in northern India and parts of the Doti region in Western Nepal.
 
 
 
• It is basically a sword dance accompanying a marriage procession but now it is performed on many auspicious occasions.
 
• ​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mukhota Dance is a dance form in which the participants wear traditional dresses and masks representing their deities and evil demons and highlighting various folk tales and the culture of Uttarakhand.
 
• Jhora dance is a springtime celebration performed by the local people by moving around in circles and highly popular dance in the Kumaon Himalayas.
 
 
• The USP of this dance is that it aims to break caste barriers, thus allowing both higher and lower caste people to perform it together.
 
 
 
• Pandav Lila or Pandav Nritya is a ritual re-enactment of stories from the Hindu epic Mahabharata, through singing, dancing and recitation, that is practised in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand.

99

questions.question: The ‘Sorrow of Bengal’ is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Damodar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Damodar River:
 
• It was earlier known as the" River of Sorrows" as it used to flood many areas Of Bardhaman, Hooghly, Howrah, and Medinipur districts.
 
• Even now the floods sometimes affect the lower Damodar Valley, but the Havoc it wreaked in earlier years is now a matter of history. 
 
• Physical Characteristics 
 
 
• Source Location- Chulha Pani ( Chandwa/Tori), Latehar, Chota Nagpur Plateau(Jharkhand)
 
• Mouth location- Hooghly river, Howrah district, (West Bengal)
 
• Length- 592 km 
 
 
 
• Tributaries
 
 
• Left Tributaries- Barakar, Konar, Jamuna
 
• Right Tributaries- Sali (West Bengal)​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Narmada**

 
 
• The Narmada is a river that originates in the **Amarkantak hills** of Madhya Pradesh, India and flows through the states of **Madhya Pradesh**, **Maharashtra**, and **Gujarat** before emptying into the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• It is the **fifth-largest **river in India, with a length of approximately **1,312 kilometers**.
 
 
 
• **The Koshi**
 
 
• The Koshi is a** transboundary **river that originates in **Tibet**.
 
• It is also known as the **Saptakoshi River**, meaning "Seven Rivers" in Sanskrit, as it is formed by the convergence of seven smaller rivers in** Nepal**.
 
• The Koshi River is known for its unpredictable and destructive nature, and it is often called the "**sorrow of Bihar**" due to the frequent floods that cause significant damage to the state of **Bihar in India**. 
 
 
 
• **The Tapi**
 
 
• The Tapi river, also known as the** Tapti**, is a major river in central India that originates in the **Satpura Range** of Madhya Pradesh and flows through **Maharashtra** and **Gujarat** before emptying into the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• The river basin is home to several large dams, including the** Ukai Dam **in **Gujarat**.

questions.question: The first bullet train project in India aims to run a bullet train at 320 kmph along a high-speed rail (HSR) track between _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ahmedabad and Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Ahmedabad and Mumbai bullet train project**

 
 
• The Ahmedabad and Mumbai High-Speed Rail project was jointly inaugurated by the **Prime Ministers of India and Japan**, **Narendra Modi **and **Shinzo Abe**, in September **2017**.
 
• The two leaders laid the foundation stone for the project at a ceremony held in **Ahmedabad**.
 
• The first bullet train project in India, officially known as the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (**MAHSR**).
 
• The project aims to run a bullet train at **320 kmph **along a high-speed rail (HSR) track between the cities of Mumbai and Ahmedabad, covering a distance of approximately **508 km**.
 
• The project is expected to reduce travel time between the two cities from the current 7-8 hours to just** 2-3 hours**.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of vinegar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CH3COOH**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vinegar **(**CH3COOH**)

 
 
• Vinegar is also known as **acetic acid** or **sour wine**.
 
• Vinegar is a sour-tasting liquid that is commonly used as a condiment in cooking and food preparation.
 
• There are several types of vinegar available, each with a unique flavor and usage.
 
• For example,** balsamic vinegar** is made from **grapes** and is commonly used in Italian cuisine.
 
• Apple **cider vinegar** is made from **apples **and is used in several cuisines.
 
• Rice vinegar is commonly used in **Asian cuisine.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **​HCOOH**

 
 
• HCOOH is the chemical formula for** formic acid**.
 
• It is an organic acid that occurs naturally in some** insects** and **plants**, such as **ants **and** stinging nettles**.
 
 
 
• **(COOH)2**
 
 
• (COOH)2 is the chemical formula for **oxalic acid**.
 
• It is a weak acid and is highly** soluble in water**.
 
 
 
• **C6H5COOH**
 
 
• C6H5COOH is the chemical formula for **benzoic acid**.
 
• It is a **white crystalline organic compound**.
 
• Benzoic acid is widely used in the** food**, **cosmetic**, and **pharmaceutical industries**.

questions.question: Which measuring instrument consists of a metal triangular frame supported on three legs, used to measure the radius of curvature of an object such as lenses and curved mirrors which are spherical in shape?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spherometer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Spherometer**

 
 
• A spherometer is a precision instrument used to **measure** the **radius of curvature of a spherical surface**.
 
• It is commonly used in fields such as optics and mechanical engineering to measure the radii of curvature of **lenses**, **mirrors**, and other **curved surfaces**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/03590750a1ca92f27a05c058ea0cf278e3db6ec8dd9f297a1f58751598822e0c.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Viscometer**

 
 
• A viscometer is an instrument used to measure the **viscosity** or **flow properties of fluids**. 
 
• There are many different types of viscometers, including **capillary viscometers**,** rotational viscometers**, and **falling ball viscometers**.
 
• They help to determine the **shear rate**, **shear stress**, and **yield stress** **of fluids**, which are used to predict how they will behave under various conditions.
 
 
 
• **Verniercaliper**
 
 
• A Vernier caliper is a precision measuring instrument used to measure the** internal **and **external dimensions** of an object with **high accuracy**.
 
• It consists of **two scales**, the **main scale**, and the **Vernier scale.**
 
• The **main scale** of the Vernier caliper is typically marked in **millimeters** or **inches.**
 
• The **Vernier scale** is a secondary scale that slides along the main scale and has smaller graduations, allowing for more precise readings.
 
 
 
• **Screw gauge**
 
 
• A screw gauge, also known as a **micrometer screw gauge**, is a precision measuring tool used to measure the **diameter of small objects** with high accuracy.
 
• It consists of a **C-shaped frame**, **a spindle**, **a thimble**, and** a screw**.

questions.question: In cricket, if the umpire raises an index finger above the head it means __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**batsman is out**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In cricket, when the umpire raises their index finger above their head, it means that the **batsman is out**.
 
• This signal is commonly known as the "**out**" signal or the "**dismissal**" signal.
 
• This can happen in a number of ways, **including being bowled**, **caught**,** stumped**, or** run out**.
 
• The umpire's decision to give an "out" signal is based on a set of rules and guidelines, which are designed to ensure fairness and consistency in the game.
 
• The decision is typically made after careful observation and consideration of the circumstances of the **dismissal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cricket**

 
 
• Cricket is a popular sport played in many countries around the world, particularly in countries like **India**, **England**, **Australia**, and **South Africa**.
 
• It is a bat-and-ball game played between two teams of eleven players each, with each team taking turns to** bat **and **bowl**.
 
• The game is played on a **circular **or **oval-shaped field**, with a rectangular **22-yard-long pitch **in the center.
 
• The pitch is divided into **two halves**, with each team taking turns to** bat** and **bowl** on each half.

questions.question: The duration of the Mesolithic period is from about ______ years ago to ______ years ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12000, 10000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Stone Age is divided into three periods, namely-
 
• Paleolithic or Old Stone Age, 2) Mesolithic or Middle Stone Age, and 3) Neolithic or New Stone Age.
 
• The word lithic is derived from the Greek lithos, meaning stone. Paleolithic means Old Stone Age, Mesolithic means Middle Stone Age, and Neolithic means New Stone Age.
 
• Mesolithic Age-
 
 
• The Mesolithic Era began about 12,000 years ago and went on for about 2,000 years.
 
• Also called the Middle Stone Age.
 
• The mesolithic Age was a much shorter period than the Palaeolithic, having lasted about ten thousand years in India.
 
• The technological hallmark of this period is tiny stone tools or microliths.
 
• In addition, the Mesolithic people also used non-microlithic tools made of flakes and blades.
 
 
 
• Microliths
 
 
• Microliths are stone tools which are of length from 1cm to 5 cm, these are shaped like blades and are made of stones such as – chert, chalcedony, agate etc.
 
• These tools are really small and sharp and have been found in different kinds of shapes such as triangles, crescents, trapezes, rhombus etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• Paleolithic Age: Paleolithic Age was developed in the Pleistocene period. 

 
 
• Robert Bruce Foote was the first person to discover a Paleolithic Stone in India in 1863.
 
• The tools of this period were made of hard rock 'quartzite' and hence people this age was called "Quartzite Man".
 
• 'Palaeo' means Old and 'Lithic' means Stone. There was basically a Hunting and food-gathering culture
 
 

 
• Neolithic Age: Le Mesurier discover the tools and implementation of the Neolithic Age.
 
 
• Neolithic-Chalcolithic Culture as a Self Sufficient food economy was defined by V. Gardon Childe.
 
• Agriculture, Domestication of Animals, and polished and grinned stone tools were practices of this age.

questions.question: In July 2022, the government prohibited the import of which of the following in line with the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021 and The Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human embryo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On July 20, 2022,** Union government** restricted the import of **human embryos** in accordance with the** Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021** and Assisted Reproductive Technology** (Regulation) Act, 2021**.
 
• Before this, such imports were restricted or prohibited **except for research purposes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Embryo**

 
 
• An embryo grows into a baby by the "Mitosis division".
 
• Mitosis involves the division of "body cells".
 
• Meiosis involves the division of "sex cells".
 
• In mitosis cell division, a cell divides into two cells that are similar to each other and have the same number of chromosomes.
 
• In meiosis cell division, a cell divides into four cells, and the number of chromosomes is halved. 
 
• The mitosis division process has the following stages such as prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, and cytokinesis.
 
 
 
• **​Women’s egg**
 
 
• Women's egg cells which are necessary for reproduction are also called **ovum**.
 
• Oocytes are immature **egg cells**.
 
• Sperm is the male **germ cell**.
 
• **Ovaries** are female sex organs. 
 
 

 
• **Stem cell**

 
 
• Stem cells are undifferentiated or partially differentiated cells in multicellular animals that can specialize in many types of cells and multiply endlessly to produce additional stem cells.
 
• In a cell lineage, they are the earliest form of cell.
 
• Tissue-specific stem cells (also referred to as somatic or adult stem cells) are more specialized than embryonic stem cells.
 
 
 
• **Kidney**
 
 
• The kidneys are two bean-shaped organs in our renal system.
 
• Kidneys comprise a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, a urinary bladder, and a urethra.
 
• Kidneys are located on either side of the backbone on the posterior surface.
 
• The kidneys perform many vital functions, including maintaining overall balance fluid, regulating, verifying & filtering minerals from the blood, etc.

questions.question: Who among the following Kathak dancers were conferred with the Padma Shri Award,2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kamalini Asthana and Nalini Asthana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The President of India bestowed PADMA SHRI on duo Nalini-Kamalini Asthana (Kathak), R Muthukannammal (Sadir), Padmaja Reddy (Kuchipudi) at a special function at Rashtrapathi Bhavan, New Delhi.
 
• Kamalini Asthana and Nalini Asthana are a sister duo from Agra in Uttar Pradesh known for their great performances of the Benaras Gharana style of Kathak.
 
• They are also known for their contributions to the popularisation of the Benaras Gharana style of Kathak both in India and abroad.
 
• In the year 2022, Govt of India conferred the Padma shri award, the third highest award in the Padma series of awards, on Kamalini Asthana and Nalini Asthana for their distinguished service in the field of art.
 
• The award is in recognition of his service as an "Acclaimed Kathak Dancer Duo from Agra known for teaching and propagating it globally".​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Awards**

 
 
• Padma Awards one of the highest civilian Awards in the country are conferred in three categories, namely, Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.
 
• The Awards are given in various disciplines/ fields of activities,
 
 
• Art, social work, public affairs, science and engineering, trade and industry, medicine, literature and education, sports, civil service, etc.
 
 
 
• Padma Vibhushan is awarded for exceptional and distinguished service.
 
• Padma Bhushan for distinguished service of a high order.
 
• Padma Shri for distinguished service in any field.
 
• The awards are announced on the occasion of Republic Day every year. 
 
• These awards are conferred by the President of India.
